meta.note: Q3 2026 proposed marks for the valuation committee

bridge.label: New rounds
bridge.note: Priced rounds and extensions that reset the mark upward

bridge.label: IPO / listing
bridge.note: Positions that became listed, or already were, and are marked to the measurement-date market cap

bridge.label: Announced deals
bridge.note: Signed but unclosed acquisitions, probability-weighted; and deals that fell through, reverted

bridge.label: Bridge notes
bridge.note: HC's new money into convertible notes, carried at cost; notes repaid in cash

bridge.label: Secondary sales
bridge.note: Partial sales and purchases; the stake held is re-marked at the last round

bridge.label: Down rounds & recaps
bridge.note: Priced rounds below the prior post-money

bridge.label: Exits realized
bridge.note: Closed acquisitions: the mark goes to zero and cash comes back

bridge.label: Write-offs
bridge.note: Shutdowns with little or no recovery

actions.action: Confirm the 30 Sep closing price, then ratify or change the 0% lock-up discount.
actions.message: The position is now listed, so the mark comes from a market capitalisation rather than a funding round, and it should be the closing price on 2026-09-30 — not the $3,931M the shares priced at on listing day. HC also cannot sell until 2027-03-19. ASC 820 disfavors blockage discounts for a Level 1 holding, so policy applies 0%, but that is a committee call rather than an arithmetic one.
points: Now **listed**: the mark is the **2026-09-30 close**, not the $3,931M listing-day price.
HC **cannot sell until 2027-03-19**.
Policy applies a **0%** lock-up discount (ASC 820 disfavors blockage on Level 1) — a committee call, not arithmetic.

suggestions.label: Book the 30 Sep close with the 0% lock-up discount, as proposed.
reasons: Level 1: the quoted price is fair value under ASC 820.
Blockage discounts on quoted prices are disfavored.

actions.action: Read the round documents and confirm the preference stack before booking this mark.
actions.message: Recap: the round priced at $37.0M against $71.0M last time. Ownership × post-money ignores liquidation preference and pay-to-play, which rounds like this almost always carry, so this figure is a ceiling on what the common equity is worth rather than an estimate of it. The terms are in the round documents, not the workbook.
points: Recap: priced at **$37.0M** against $71.0M last round.
Ownership × post-money **ignores liquidation preference** and pay-to-play.
So the mark is a **ceiling**, not an estimate — the terms sit in the round documents.

suggestions.label: Book the recap figure as proposed.
reasons: It is the only priced transaction and reflects the new capital structure.
The preference stack can only lower it — a ceiling beats a stale higher mark.

suggestions.label: Hold the prior mark until the round documents are read.
reasons: Defers the write-down until the preference terms are known.
Overstates if the round closed as priced — only if documents arrive before the close.

decisions.event: Acquisition (Announced) · Definitive agreement signed, all cash

actions.action: Ratify the 0.90 close probability, or choose full deal value or hold at prior.
actions.message: A buyer has signed for $133M but the deal has not closed and still needs approval. Booking the full deal value ignores that contingency; holding the old mark ignores a signed agreement. Policy splits the difference at 0.90, giving $4.31M against $4.79M at full value and $3.50M if held.
points: Buyer signed for **$133M**, but the deal has **not closed** and still needs approval.
Policy weights it at **0.90** → **$4.31M**.
Alternatives: **$4.79M** at full value, **$3.50M** held at prior.

suggestions.label: Ratify the 0.90-weighted mark of $4.31M.
reasons: Reflects a signed agreement with a real chance of not closing.
Policy default for an announced, unclosed deal.

suggestions.label: Book the full deal value, $4.79M.
reasons: The buyer has signed; only approval remains.
Right if the closing conditions are formalities.

suggestions.label: Hold the prior mark, $3.50M, until the deal closes.
reasons: Nothing is realised until closing; a signed deal can still break.
Right if approval is uncertain or the buyer is stretched.

decisions.event: Convertible Note · $4.7M bridge note, $133.0M valuation cap

actions.action: Confirm the $0.50M is carried at cost, and whether the bridge signals distress.
actions.message: HC put $0.50M into a bridge note (cap $133.0M, +80% vs last round). The equity mark cannot move — a cap is a ceiling on a future conversion price, not a price — so the new money is carried separately at cost until the note converts.
points: **$0.50M** into a bridge note (cap $133.0M, +80% vs last round).
A cap is a **ceiling on a future conversion**, not a price — the equity mark cannot move.
The new money is carried **separately at cost** until it converts.

suggestions.label: Carry the note at cost beside the unchanged equity mark, as proposed.
reasons: A cap is not a price; cost is the only observable value for the note.
Standard treatment until the note converts.

suggestions.label: Treat the bridge as distress: carry equity only, note written to zero.
reasons: A bridge instead of a priced round often means the company cannot raise.
Conservative; reverses on conversion.
